rows.en: Run away

I snatched up a shard of the glass that had shattered when I broke the cabinet.
"Ow!"
In my hurry, I'd cut my hand.
But I couldn't worry about that right now.
"Yaaah!"
I thrust the glass shard at him, out of my mind.{p}

"Owww!"
The glass shard sliced Hosoda's ear clean off.
"It hurts! It hurts! My ear, my ear!"
Hosoda clutched his left ear, tumbling and rolling on the floor.
Hosoda's left ear lay at my feet.{p}What will you do?
Act tough
Apologize
Comfort him
Run off
"Quit your bawling!"{p}

I kicked Hosoda hard in the side as he rolled around.
"Gaahk!"
Disgustingly, Hosoda threw up his half-digested food.
Then I grabbed Hosoda by the hair and yanked his face up as hard as I could.
"How many people have you killed so far, you bastard?! You murderer!
And yet the moment you get hurt yourself, you start crying.
Cry any more and I'll slice off your other ear too!"
I was burning with a rage I couldn't put into words.
Whenever I thought of how this guy had killed so many innocent people, I was so angry I couldn't stand it.
Maybe my threat had worked; Hosoda curled up his huge body and began to shake.
At least he seemed to have stopped crying.
He was desperately sniffling back his snot, trying not to cry.{p}What will you do?
Punch him flying
Ask why he's trying to kill me
Ask where the ampoule is
Let him get away
Tie him up
Ask about the Murder Club

"You'll get killed even if you cry.
I just saw Kazama dead. Hino killed him.
I tied up Shindo, but he's probably dead by now, isn't he?
...And Arai and Iwashita are dead too.
Do you want to die too?"
My words must have been a huge shock to him.
After that, Hosoda started blabbing away, even about things I hadn't asked.{p}
"Help me! Protect me! I'll tell you anything.
"Help me! Forgive me! I'll tell you anything.

The Murder Club has been around for a long time.
I don't know the details myself, but it never acts out in the open.
Because it's an underground club.
You get it, right? Right? Right?
So, anyway, the current president is Lord Hino.
At this school, anyone who goes against Lord Hino gets killed. Every one of them.
There are only seven members in the club right now, but they're all scary people.
...I know! I'll ask Lord Hino for you.
So you can become a member of the Murder Club. How about it? Sounds good, right?
That way you won't have to die either. And we can all get together and kill anyone we don't like.
Right? Let's do that. Right? Right?"{p}

There are only three members left, him included...
Wouldn't Hino want more members right about now?{p}
What should I do?
Get them to let you join the Murder Club

rows.en: Refuse to join something like that

"Don't get cute with me. Look who you're talking to!
Say something that stupid again and I'll fucking kill you!"
I waved the bloodstained glass right in front of Hosoda's eyes.
"I'm sorry! I'm sorry!
I didn't mean it like that!
That's right, you're not the kind of person who'd join a club like this, are you?
Instead, I'll tell you where the ampoule is. So please, forgive me."{p}

"Y-Yeah, yeah, yeah!"
Hosoda nodded over and over.
It seemed he really did know.
"If you're lying, I'll fucking kill you!"
Hosoda shook his head hard.
"I'm not lying. I'll do anything, if you'll just save me.
The ampoule is in the old school building.
You see, I saw Lord Hino going to hide it in the old school building.
I don't know where, but I'm sure it's in the old school building."
"...The old school building, huh."
"...Oh! You have to keep this a secret, no matter what.
Otherwise they'll kill me. Please."
I shoved Hosoda away as he clung to me.{p}
"...The old school building."

I had to hurry.
...But was there anywhere I needed to go first?{p}Where will you go?
Chemistry lab
Art room
Nurse's office
Gym
Old school building
Staff room
Night-duty room
Other
Classroom
Restroom
School gate
Flower bed
Home economics room
Newspaper club room
Library
Other

I headed straight for the old school building.
"Please! Don't tell, okay? You have to keep me out of it, no matter what!"
Hosoda was shouting behind me.
But I had no time to waste on a guy like that.
I had to hurry to the old school building.{p}

I rushed into the old school building.
It was dark, just as I'd expected.
Normally, I'd never come to a place like this alone.
But this was no time to be saying things like that.
I switched on my flashlight.{p}
The old school building had three floors.{p}Where will you go?
First-floor classrooms
First-floor restroom
Second-floor classrooms
Second-floor restroom
Third-floor classrooms
Third-floor restroom
Leave the old school building
I decided to go to the classrooms on the first floor of the old school building.{p}

The hallway floor looked like it could give way any second.
But I couldn't let that stop me.
Even in the old school building, there were seven classrooms on each floor.{p}Which classroom will you go to?
Far left
Second from left
Third from left
Fourth from left
Fifth from left
Sixth from left
Far right
Search elsewhere
I decided to go to the classroom on the far left.{p}

I went into the classroom and shone my flashlight around inside.
Only a few scattered desks were left.
It didn't look like searching would take long.
First, I checked the teacher's platform.
...Nothing.
Next, I checked the remaining desks.
I searched every inch inside the desks, too.
...Nothing.
I searched every inch of the room, corner to corner.
It didn't seem to be in this classroom.{p}
Where should I go?
I decided to go to the second classroom from the left.{p}

I went into the classroom and shone my flashlight around inside.
Only a few scattered desks were left.
It didn't look like searching would take long.
First, I checked the teacher's platform.
...Nothing.
Next, I checked the remaining desks.
I searched every inch inside the desks, too.
...Nothing.
I searched every inch of the room, corner to corner.
It didn't seem to be in this classroom.{p}
Where should I go?
I decided to go to the third classroom from the left.{p}

I went into the classroom and shone my flashlight around inside.
Only a few scattered desks were left.
It didn't look like searching would take long.
First, I checked the teacher's platform.
...Nothing.
Next, I checked the remaining desks.
I searched every inch inside the desks, too.
...Huh?
There's something here.
What is this?{p}

"Whoa!"
...It was a dead rat.
...Phew, that nearly gave me a heart attack.
There was nothing in the desks.
I searched every inch of the room, corner to corner.
It didn't seem to be in this classroom.{p}
Where should I go?
That's enough of the first-floor classrooms for now.{p}
Where should I go?

rows.en:
I decided to go to the first-floor restroom.
There was a boys' restroom and a girls' restroom.{p}Which one will you search?
Boys' restroom
Girls' restroom
Search elsewhere

I decided to search the first-floor boys' restroom.
What a filthy restroom, though.
The boys' restroom had four urinals and two stalls.
...I didn't really want to search in here, but my life was on the line.{p}Where should I search?
The urinals
The back stall
The front stall
Search elsewhere

I shone the light on the row of four urinals.
Ugh...!
They were crawling with cockroaches.
The moment the light hit them, they all scattered at once.
I searched carefully, but it didn't seem to be here.{p}Where should I search?
I decided to check the stall at the back.{p}

...Surely it wouldn't be inside the toilet bowl itself.
I searched every inch.{p}
...Nothing.{p}
Where should I search?
I decided to search somewhere else.{p}
What should I do?
Where should I go?

rows.en:
I decided to go to the third-floor restrooms.
There was a boys' restroom and a girls' restroom.{p}Which one should I check?
Boys' restroom
Girls' restroom
Search elsewhere

The girls' restroom had four stalls.
I remembered hearing a rumor that Hanako-san haunted the girls' restroom in the old school building.
But right now, nothing could scare me.
Time was slipping away fast.{p}Where should I search?
The back stall
Second from the back
Third from the back
The front stall
Search elsewhere
I decided to search the stall at the very back.{p}

I shone the light.
Then I searched every inch of the back stall.
...Nothing.
No good.
I'd better search somewhere else.{p}
Where should I search?
I decided to search the second stall from the back.{p}

I shone the light.
Then I searched every inch of the second stall from the back.
...Nothing.
No good.
No, wait!
Something was sitting on the ledge of the stall's frame.
I shone my flashlight on it.{p}

It was an ampoule filled with a yellow liquid.
I found it!
That's it!
I finally found it!
I reached out for it.{p}

"Kyeeeeeeeee!"
A shrill scream suddenly rang out, and the next instant something slammed into my back.
"Aaagh!"
Something was stuck in my shoulder.
I pulled it out. It was a mechanical pencil.
"Die! Just die!"
Someone was strangling me.
The flashlight had slipped from my hand and rolled away, and its beam lit up my attacker's face.{p}

It was Fukuzawa.
"Let go!"
I shoved Fukuzawa away.
But she wouldn't let go.
"Aaagh!"
A searing pain shot across my face.
Fukuzawa had clawed me with her sharp nails.
I covered my face without thinking.
Fukuzawa sank her teeth into my hand.
...Damn it!
I was just one step away!{p}What do I do?!
Strangle Fukuzawa back
Use that report
Pick up the mechanical pencil
Run away for now
I read out the title of that report.{p}If I remember right, the title was...
One Hundred Days in Human Life and Death
A Hundred-Day Period of Human Life and Death
Trends of Human Life and Death Over a Hundred-Day Period
Trends in Human Life and Death Over One Hundred Days
Trends in Human Life and Death Over a Hundred-Day Period

"How do you know that★"
It was too dark to read, but I thrust the report in my hand out in front of Fukuzawa.
"I found this in the chemistry lab! You're a horrible girl.
Though any teacher who'd accept something like this is just as bad."
"Give it back!"
Fukuzawa tried to snatch the report away.
But I wasn't going to hand it over that easily.
"Whoa there! Is this so important to you?!"
I slipped out of Fukuzawa's grasp and held the report up high.
"Give it back to me!"
That report must have meant the world to Fukuzawa.
Of course it did.
It was an outrageous report that set out to record a human being's life right up until the moment of death.
"Ah!"
Fukuzawa clawed me, and the report fell from my hand.
Caught by the wind, the report fluttered up and flew out the window.{p}

"My report!"
"Look out!"{p}
"Kyaaaaaaaaah☆"{p}

Just as Fukuzawa reached out the window, the window frame snapped.
The wood of the frame had rotted through.
Along with dozens of pure white sheets of paper, Fukuzawa's body flew out into the air.
Even as she fell, Fukuzawa glared up at me, spitting out some kind of curse.
A sickening thud rang out, the sound of something heavy smashing into the ground, and I leaned out the window.
Carefully, so I wouldn't fall...{p}

Below, Fukuzawa lay spread-eagled on the ground.
Her neck was twisted at an impossible angle.
It was broken clean through.
In the moonlight, the report pages fluttered down onto her white sailor uniform like confetti.
The report chronicling life and death, never to be finished, kept piling up on top of Fukuzawa.
Perhaps Fukuzawa had completed her report with her own death.
...That's right.
I couldn't just stand around like this.{p}

I took deep breath after deep breath, then checked my watch again.
The appointed time had already passed.
...I was alive.
I was saved!
Tears spilled down my cheeks on their own.
So this was how wonderful it was to be alive.
For the first time in my life, I savored the joy of being alive.
...Thank God.
I let out another sigh.{p}What should I do?
Wait here until morning?
Or go home?
Wait here until morning
Go home

Once I knew I was saved, the fear suddenly came flooding back stronger than before.
This was the old school building, in the dead of night.
I was far too frightened to wait in a place like this until morning.
I picked up the flashlight that had been knocked out of my hand and stood up.
Then, without really thinking, my eyes fell on the broken window frame.
Rotten, crumbling wood.
But it still seemed fairly sturdy.
An idea came to me.
...This might come in handy.
I picked up the broken piece of window frame.
Perhaps that was nothing less than a warning from God.{p}

...I felt dizzy.
Exhaustion crashed down on me all at once.
Still, I couldn't believe how much I'd managed to do.
I was impressed by my own stamina.
Staggering, I slowly put one leaden leg in front of the other.{p}

Going down the stairs was agony.
With every step, I felt like my foot was about to slip.
There was no strength left in my legs at all.
By the time I finally made it down to the first floor, the sky was about to start turning pale.{p}

...And then.
There he stood, in front of the school gate.
Arms folded, he seemed to have been lying in wait for me.
"...Hino."
"You've really put up a fight, {a}.
I've played this human-hunting game plenty of times, but this is a first.
What do you say? Why don't you run the Murder Club with me?"
Hino smiled, his face perfectly pleasant.{p}

"............Don't be stupid. I'd sooner die."
"...I see. That's a shame.
I thought you'd make a good partner.
I've disposed of all the traitors.
Kazama, Shindo, Hosoda too. There's no one left.
And I'm graduating soon.
I thought you could take over after me and make a fine club president.
Well? Won't you reconsider?"
"No way."
"So stubborn. Well, it can't be helped. Then I'll give up on you.
The Murder Club ends with me."{p}

As we talked, I moved step by step toward the school gate where Hino was waiting.
"Hino. There's one thing I want to ask you."
"What is it?"
"What is a Murder Club even for?"
"I'm so glad you asked.
You see, people build up this thing called stress. But the elite must never let stress build up.
So what do you do about it?
That's right. You eliminate anything that might cause you stress.
You kill every last person who makes you angry.
That way, stress never builds up, and whatever stress you have just naturally melts away.
It's fun. Is there any other method as wonderful as this?"
"You're out of your mind."
"...Thank you. I'll take that as a compliment.
In every age, ordinary people never understand what a genius thinks.
Now, let's bring this to an end."{p}

Hino pulled out a knife.
I probably didn't even have the strength left to dodge.
Without a word, I thrust my hand into my pocket.
In my pocket was...{p}

Then Hino charged at me, swinging the knife.
There was only one path left to me...{p}What do I do?
Fall down on purpose
Deliberately let Hino stab me with his knife
Take out the screwdriver in my pocket
Apologize
Say I'll join the Murder Club

"Come on, Hino! Don't miss! Drive that knife into my gut as hard as you can!"
I shouted.
"Heh, giving up, are you?!"
Hino charged at me, laughing.
I focused every nerve I had on Hino's knife.
This was my last gamble.
If my luck held, it was sure to work.
It mustn't miss.
I had to take Hino's knife in exactly the right spot.{p}

If it missed... I'd die!
"Let me put you out of your misery!"{p}

"Ngh!"
A dull pain throbbed through my stomach.{p}

The next moment, a look of dismay spread across Hino's face.
For Hino, this was something that should never have happened.
"You bastard... You tricked me."
"What's wrong, Hino? You've gone deathly pale."
With my left hand, I gripped Hino's hand, knife and all, where it was thrust into my stomach.
And with my right, I fumbled the screwdriver out of my pocket.{p}There wasn't a moment to lose.
What do I do?
Drive the screwdriver into Hino's throat
Drive the screwdriver into Hino's heart
Drive the screwdriver into Hino's shoulder
Without hesitating, I drove the screwdriver into Hino's shoulder.{p}

"Gyaah!"
Hino went tumbling to the ground.{p}

Hino's knife was still sticking out of my stomach.
I pulled the knife out.
...There wasn't a single drop of blood on it.
Because I had hidden the broken window frame from the old school building's restroom inside my dress shirt. The screwdriver was buried in Hino's shoulder.
He was clutching his stabbed shoulder, shielding it.
Blood was faintly seeping through.{p}
